'''Xu Xurong''' ({{zh|c=徐叙瑢|p=Xú Xùróng}}; 23 April 1922 – 12 July 2022) was a Chinese physicist, and an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He was a delegate to the [[12th National People's Congress]].

==Biography==
Xu was born in [[Linyi|Linyi County]] (now Linyi), [[Shandong]], on 23 April 1922.<ref name="ap">{{cite news|url=https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2022-07-14/2363878.html |script-title=zh:痛别！我国发光学科奠基人徐叙瑢院士逝世 |work=nbd.com.cn |date=14 July 2022 |access-date=14 July 2022 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="bee">{{cite news|author1=Li Jingtong ({{lang|zh|李京统}})|url=https://www.bjnews.com.cn/detail/1657716254168066.html |script-title=zh:徐叙瑢院士逝世 |work=Beijing News |date=13 July 2022 |access-date=14 July 2022 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="ceramic">{{cite news|author1=Yue Huairang ({{lang|zh|岳怀让}})|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_18995480 |script-title=zh:中科院院士徐叙瑢逝世，共和国今年已痛失20位两院院士 |work=thepaper.cn |date=13 July 2022 |access-date=14 July 2022 |language=zh}}</ref> He attended Confucius Temple School ({{zh|s=孔子庙小学|labels=no}}). After the outbreak of the [[Second Sino-Japanese War]], he escaped to [[central China]]'s [[Hubei]] province, where he studied at Yunyang National Shandong Middle School ({{zh|s=郧阳国立山东中学|labels=no}}), then fled to [[southwest China]]'s [[Sichuan]] province, and studied in Mianyang National No. 6 High School (now Mianyang Nanshan High School; {{zh|s=绵阳南山中学|labels=no}}). In 1941, he was admitted to [[National Southwestern Associated University]], majoring in [[physics]].<ref name="ap"/><ref name="bee"/><ref name="ceramic"/> After graduating in 1945, he became an assistant at [[Peking University]] and was a graduate student under the supervision of [[Rao Yutai]]. In 1950, he was transferred to the Institute of Physics of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] to engage in solid-state luminescence research. One year later, he was sent to study at the [[Lebedev Physical Institute]], earning his vice-doctorate degree in 1955.<ref name="ap"/><ref name="bee"/><ref name="ceramic"/>

In September 1965, adjusted by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, [[Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics]] was established with luminescence as its main research direction.<ref name="bee"/> In 1966, Xu was assigned to the institute, where he was promoted to director in 1978 and honorary director after 1985.<ref name="bee"/> In 1980, Xu, together with Xu Shaohong ({{zh|s=许少鸿|labels=no}}), Wu Boxuan ({{zh|s=吴伯僖|labels=no}}) and others, jointly founded the Luminescence Branch Society of the [[Chinese Physical Society]] and served as its first president. In 1987, he moved to Tianjin Institute of Technology (now [[Tianjin University of Technology]]), where he established the Institute of Material Physics as director. In 1997, he joined the faculty of [[Beijing Jiaotong University|Northern Jiaotong University]] (now Beijing Jiaotong University) and established the research base of Luminescence, the Institute of Optoelectronic Technology.<ref name="bee"/>

On 12 July 2022, Xu died from an illness in [[Beijing]], at the age of 100.<ref name="ap"/><ref name="bee"/><ref name="ceramic"/>

==Honours and awards==
* 1980 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS)
* 1999 Science and Technology Progress Award of the [[Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation]]
